acceptance_criteria.criterion: packages/core publicly exports distinct Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, and Tick types; cross-brand assignment fails compile-time type test.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: packages/core/src/numeric.type-test.mts declares CrossBrandNegativeAssertions and TickCrossBrandNegativeAssertions covering all 12 pair combinations among the four bigint brands plus all 8 Tick-vs-bigint-brand assertions using Expect<NotAssignable<A,B>>; verified the mechanism catches assignability by temporarily replacing one entry with NotAssignable<Money,Money> which produced tsc error TS2344 as expected.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Money, Quantity, Price, Rate use bigint underlying representation; Tick uses number underlying representation.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: numeric.mts declares Money/Quantity/Price/Rate as `bigint & { brand }` and Tick as `number & { brand }`; runtime test QUANTITY_SCALE typeof bigint plus Money(0n) returning bigint and Tick(0) returning number confirm the underlying primitives.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Tick accepts safe integers in [MIN_SAFE_INTEGER, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER] and rejects fractional, NaN, infinities, and out-of-range values.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Tests in tests/core/numeric.test.mjs cover Tick(MIN_SAFE_INTEGER), Tick(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER), Tick(MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1) throws, Tick(MIN_SAFE_INTEGER-1) throws, Tick(1.5)/Tick(0.1)/Tick(-1.5) throw, Tick(NaN)/Tick(POSITIVE_INFINITY)/Tick(NEGATIVE_INFINITY) throw. Constructor uses Number.isSafeInteger which is exact for this predicate.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Runtime constructors reject wrong primitive types; no runtime detection of erased TypeScript brands required.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Each of Money/Quantity/Price/Rate rejects number, string, null, undefined, boolean, object, and symbol via typeof !== 'bigint' guard; Tick rejects bigint, string, null, undefined, boolean, object via typeof !== 'number' guard; no runtime cross-brand check is performed.

notes_for_reviewer: Branded types use `declare const XxxBrand: unique symbol` phantom keys; the symbols never exist at runtime. This ensures cross-brand assignments are distinguished structurally by TypeScript and cannot be forged from another module.

The repository did not previously have a TypeScript type-test mechanism. Introduced a minimal one (Expect<T extends true> plus NotAssignable<From,To>) inside packages/core/src/numeric.type-test.mts. The file uses `import type` only so it emits an empty `export {};` module.

Tick constructor uses a single Number.isSafeInteger check because that predicate is exactly false for fractional, non-finite, and out-of-safe-range values; a separate typeof check precedes it to distinguish wrong-primitive errors (NUMERIC_WRONG_PRIMITIVE) from out-of-range errors (NUMERIC_TICK_OUT_OF_RANGE).

ADR-001 constrains Tick to non-negative values, but the task explicitly requests the [MIN_SAFE_INTEGER, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER] range matching ADR-003. Implemented per task; higher-layer domain enforcement of non-negativity remains a future concern and is out of scope for TASK-0010.
`export { Money }` from index.mts re-exports both the type and the value binding since verbatimModuleSyntax is false in the base tsconfig.
payload.summary: Added branded numeric primitives to packages/core: distinct bigint-backed Money/Quantity/Price/Rate and number-backed Tick types with runtime constructors that validate the underlying primitive; Tick additionally rejects non-integers, out-of-safe-range values, NaN, and infinities via Number.isSafeInteger. Exposed QUANTITY_SCALE=100000000n, PRICE_SCALE=10000n, RATE_SCALE=100000000n as bigint literals with no floating-point conversion. Established a compile-time type-test mechanism (Expect/NotAssignable) covering all 12 cross-brand pairs among Money/Quantity/Price/Rate, all 8 Tick/bigint-brand cross assertions, and 5 unbranded primitive-to-brand negative assertions. Public API re-exported through packages/core/src/index.mts. No production code uses Math.random, Date, performance, crypto, floating-point arithmetic, or mutable global state.
